title: Fencepost scope & eval‑gated acceptance for hosted endpoint surface
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: The hosted endpoint product family (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) has accumulated divergent expectations across lanes: subtle behavioral guarantees, differing determinism tradeoffs, and inconsistent eval coverage. This ticket defines a compact PRD that fences scope for an MVP hosted surface, standardizes acceptance criteria tied to explicit eval slices and performance budgets, and produces a concise launch playbook that engineering and SRE can operate against.

Goals: 1) Produce a single-sourced PRD describing minimal behavioral contracts for each endpoint type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). 2) Define eval slices, quality gates, and quantitative thresholds for go/no-go. 3) Surface operational acceptance (latency, error budget, rollout slices) and migration notes for existing consumers. 4) Deliver a 1‑page launch checklist and a short runbook for canary/rollback conditions.

Out of scope: New SDK features, dedicated capacity pricing changes, and on‑prem packaging work are intentionally excluded from this scope fence. Those will be handled in follow-up tickets with explicit dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: PRD: one document per endpoint type with required fields: behavior summary, failing/acceptable examples, required telemetry, and eval slice specifications
Eval plan: at least 6 representative eval slices (production-derived) per endpoint and automated CI job that fails PR if baseline regression > 2% on any high-priority slice
Performance: 95th percentile tail latency under announced SLA for the seeded traffic profiles (detailed numbers in linked runbook)
Reliability: SRE acceptance test run and documented emergency rollback criteria (including model fallback matrix) in the runbook
Launch checklist: All items below completed and marked in the checklist file; at least one cross-functional dry run recorded
Docs & SDK: API contract examples committed to docs repo and smoke test scripts available for customer success
tasks: Write PRD sections for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank (owner per section assigned)
Define and document eval slices (data owners: PM + Research)
Create CI jobs for eval gating and hook into PR validation
Coordinate SRE on latency budgets and canary window sizing
Prepare one-page launch checklist and step-by-step cutover runbook
Schedule cross-team dry run (PM, Eng, SRE, DX, CS) and capture action items
decisions: Acceptance gating will be eval-driven with slice-level thresholds rather than human signoff for key regressions
Default fallback policy for severe quality regressions is deterministic: route affected lane traffic to prior verified model variant; throttle new sessions until rollback completes
Behavioral determinism is required for 'tiered-fastlane' customers but not default for all hosted lanes; document as lane config
tradeoffs: Tight eval gates reduce release risk but increase engineering overhead for CI and infra costs
Narrowing scope now speeds launch but requires follow-up tickets for SDK ergonomics and multi-tenant billing clarity
Favoring automated slice gates may miss rare semantic regressions; plan includes a manual review step for open-ended slices
